eips.title: Revert creation in case of non-empty storage
eips.summary: Removed from Glamsterdam tests; its removal is the reason EIP-8253 was proposed as a companion fix.

moments.context: Danceratopz noted that EIP-7610 was removed in tests-glamsterdam-devnet v8.1.3 and tests v20.0.2.
Jochem referenced EIP-684's collision check only covering nonce and code, not storage, which EIP-7610's removal exposed as an issue for BALs.
Spencer described EIP-8253 as a wrap-up after de-CFI'ing EIP-7610, noting clients ended up differing again.

Stefan gave a heads-up that state gas in debug traces for EIP-8037 would be discussed on the RPC standards call starting in seven minutes.

eips.title: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
eips.summary: Debated whether to ship with Glamsterdam or defer to Hegota; rough consensus was to defer, with final decision on Thursday.

moments.context: Danceratopz introduced the topic of shipping EIP-8253 with Glamsterdam as a companion to the EIP-7610 removal and BAL edge case.
Jochem explained the BAL incompatibility with the yellow paper's Formula 99 for accounts with zero nonce but non-empty storage, affecting 28 accounts.
Toni asked what goes wrong without it; Jochem explained that BAL state diffs would produce a different state root than re-executing transactions for these accounts.
Toni said the EIP makes sense but advocated for Hegota rather than including it this late in the Glamsterdam process.
Spencer noted this is a wrap-up after de-CFI'ing 7610, said it's easy to test, and asked client teams for their preference.
Dragan from Reth said he wants it done as fast as possible and is fine with either Glamsterdam or Hegota.
FLCL from Nethermind said it seems too late for Glamsterdam due to insufficient transition testing time, preferring Hegota.
Marius from Geth said he's fine deferring unless it creates tech debt by requiring different BAL mechanisms between Glamsterdam and Hegota.
Toni suggested delaying the final decision until Thursday's ACD call to allow async coordination among client teams.

eips.title: Revert creation in case of collision
eips.summary: Referenced as the contract collision check that only verifies nonce and code, not storage, relevant to the EIP-8253 discussion.

moments.context: Jochem cited EIP-684's collision test as only checking nonce zero and empty code, not storage, explaining why these 28 accounts are problematic.

eips.title: TCREATE Opcode
eips.summary: Jochem mentioned the TCREATE opcode as an alternative being explored for users of the self-destruct-create pattern.

moments.context: Jochem said he requested an ephemeral accounts channel on EF R&D to help users transition to EIP-8360's TCREATE opcode instead of self-destruct patterns.
